subject: dsa
title: Partition Labels
summary: Each letter must stay in one part, so a part can't end before the last occurrence of any letter inside it. Sweep right, stretching the part's end to the farthest last-occurrence seen; cut when the scan reaches that end.
problem: Partition a string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return the part sizes.

steps.caption: Cut the string into as many parts as possible, with each letter confined to one part. First record where each letter last appears.
Start a part at index 0. It must reach at least a's last occurrence, index 3, so the part can't end before there.
Scanning on, b last appears at index 5, stretching the part's end to 5. c's last index 4 already sits inside.
At index 5 the scan reaches the part's end and no letter inside points further. Cut the first part: 'abcacb', size 6.
The next part starts at index 6. 'd' appears only here, so it closes immediately as a part of size 1.
Likewise 'e' at index 7 is alone. The partition sizes are 6, 1, 1.
